traps: A promotion cannot be undone, so a fallback needs a separate reverse migration back to the source.
A heterogeneous migration changes the engine, so application code and queries must change.

confused.tell: Datastream keeps an analytics copy in BigQuery while the source stays primary, and DMS moves the primary.
Warehouse migrations into BigQuery use BigQuery Migration Service and BigQuery Data Transfer Service, not DMS.
For self-managed Redis, import RDB files from Cloud Storage into Memorystore, because DMS covers MySQL, PostgreSQL, SQL Server, and Oracle.

services.name: Storage Transfer Service
services.what: Storage Transfer Service copies data into Cloud Storage from Amazon S3, Azure Blob Storage, HTTP URLs, HDFS, and file systems. It is a managed service for large transfers, with full and incremental copies.
cues: Hundreds of terabytes on an NFS filer must move to Cloud Storage over a link that can meet the deadline.
Incremental copies must run until cutover and stay under a bandwidth limit during business hours.
Objects in Amazon S3 or Azure Blob Storage must be copied into Cloud Storage, once or on a schedule.
traps: File system transfers need agents on machines that mount the data, so plan agents in the data center.
Event-driven transfers copy new objects from S3, Azure, or Cloud Storage and cannot read an on-premises file system.

confused.tell: When the network cannot finish the transfer before the deadline, ship a Transfer Appliance instead.
BigQuery Data Transfer Service loads data into BigQuery tables, while Storage Transfer Service copies files to Cloud Storage.
To keep raw data in AWS and move only results, query it in place with BigQuery Omni.

services.name: Transfer Appliance
services.what: Transfer Appliance is Google-owned hardware that Google ships to you. You copy data to it and ship it back, and Google uploads the data to Cloud Storage.
cues: An online upload at the available bandwidth would take more than one week.
At 100 Mbps, 100 TB takes over 100 days online, and the deadline is weeks away.
More bandwidth, such as a new Interconnect connection, cannot arrive before the deadline.
A remote site has little bandwidth or poor connectivity.
traps: Transfer Appliance moves bulk data once, so it gives no continuous replication for disaster recovery.
It lands files in Cloud Storage, not schema and tables in BigQuery.

confused.tell: If the network can meet the deadline, Storage Transfer Service is the managed online choice with incremental copies.
A new Dedicated Interconnect connection can take months to install, so it cannot rescue a short transfer deadline.

services.name: BigQuery Data Transfer Service
services.what: BigQuery Data Transfer Service automates scheduled loads into BigQuery. Sources include Cloud Storage, Amazon S3, Azure Blob Storage, SaaS applications, and Teradata through a migration agent.
cues: SaaS or other-cloud data must load into BigQuery on a schedule.
A Teradata warehouse moves to BigQuery, and the team wants a managed copy of the schema and data.
traps: It cannot move data out of BigQuery.
It does not filter during the transfer, so the raw data leaves the source cloud before any SQL filter runs.

confused.tell: A scheduled load cannot give minutes of delay, while Datastream streams database changes continuously.
Storage Transfer Service copies files into Cloud Storage, while BigQuery Data Transfer Service loads tables into BigQuery.
BigQuery Omni queries S3 data in place and moves only results, while a transfer moves the raw data first.

docs.title: Introduction to the BigQuery Data Transfer Service

services.name: Committed use discounts and sustained use discounts
services.what: Committed use discounts (CUDs) lower the price for a 1-year or 3-year commitment to resources or to an hourly spend. Sustained use discounts apply automatically, but only to N1, N2, N2D, C2, M1, M2, and sole-tenant nodes.
cues: A steady baseline runs all year, and on-demand autoscaling handles the peaks.
Finance wants a predictable monthly cost and a lower unit price for stable usage.
Workloads will move across regions, machine series, GKE, and Cloud Run during the term.
A managed service such as Cloud SQL has a steady, predictable baseline.
traps: A resource-based CUD cannot be canceled, so it wastes money when the fleet moves to other regions, series, or Cloud Run.
A commitment sized to a seasonal peak sits unused most of the year, and you still pay every hour.

confused.tell: A commitment is a price agreement only, while a reservation holds zonal capacity, so buy both for discount and capacity.
Fault-tolerant batch work that runs part of the day fits Spot VMs, and flexible CUDs never cover Spot VMs.

services.aws: EC2 Reserved Instances (resource-based) and Compute Savings Plans (flexible)

docs.title: Committed use discounts (CUDs) for Compute Engine

services.name: Compute Engine reservations
services.what: A Compute Engine reservation gives high assurance of capacity in one zone. You pay the on-demand rate for the reserved resources while the reservation exists, used or not.
cues: DR VMs must be able to start in the failover zones, even when those zones are short of capacity.
Hundreds of extra VMs must start in one zone on the day of a known event.
A GPU training run has a fixed start date and lasts up to 90 days.
Large training on clustered GPUs runs for months from a known future date.
traps: Reservations cannot supply capacity for Spot VMs or preemptible VMs.
An on-demand reservation created weeks early bills for every unused week, so use a future reservation for a later date.

confused.tell: A quota only permits resource creation, and it does not guarantee that the zone has capacity.
A commitment discounts usage but reserves nothing. Create a reservation for capacity, and attach it to a resource-based commitment.
Flex-start VMs suit jobs of up to seven days that can wait for capacity, while reservations suit fixed dates.

services.name: Cloud Billing (budgets, export, FinOps hub)
services.what: Cloud Billing tracks and allocates spend with budgets, billing reports, billing export to BigQuery, and the FinOps hub. An alerts-only budget never stops spend. Only a spend cap budget (Preview) pauses a few services.
cues: Finance wants showback by team and environment inside shared projects, with resource-level cost in SQL.
Spend above a budget must trigger an automatic action, such as stopping VMs while data stays safe.
A FinOps team must manage budgets and cost exports without linking projects or changing payment settings.
A runaway Gemini API or Cloud Run service must pause at a spend limit.
traps: An alerts-only budget never stops services, so charges keep accruing past 100%.
Disabling billing stops all services in the project and can delete resources, so stop selected resources instead.

confused.tell: Quotas limit resource or API usage, not money, and they do not react to a budget.

docs.title: Create, edit, or delete budgets and budget alerts

services.name: Cloud Quotas
services.what: A quota sets the maximum amount of a resource or API that a project, or a user, can consume. It limits usage, not money, and it does not guarantee that capacity exists.
cues: Each analyst needs a daily limit on the BigQuery bytes that on-demand queries can process.
A capacity plan must make sure the DR region can take the failover load, including peaks.
API requests fail with HTTP 429, or Compute Engine returns QUOTA_EXCEEDED.
traps: A project-level BigQuery quota is one shared total, so one analyst can use it up and block the team.
API request quotas are not designed as a project-wide spending cap.

confused.tell: A quota permits resource creation but does not guarantee zonal capacity, while a reservation does.
A budget alerts on cost, while a quota blocks usage above a limit and ignores money.
A contractual daily call limit for partner APIs is an Apigee Quota policy, not a project quota.
